entries.title: CFTC publishes an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets, including a new crypto asset market subcategory of designated contract market registration
entries.facts: CFTC press release 9307-26, dated October 5, 2026, states that "The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to provide notice of, and seek public comment regarding, its intent to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework comprised of fit-for-purpose rules concerning section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act and retail commodity transactions described thereunder involving crypto assets (such transactions, \"CTXs\")." The release names two prospective rule sets, Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets, and states that the Commission intends to "codify through rulemaking a subcategory of designated contract market registration, known as a crypto asset market, that is purpose-built specifically for CTXs." It states that the ANPRM seeks input on preventing abusive practices and on providing crypto-specific compliance guidance. On timing the release states: "Comments must be in writing and received within 60 days of the ANPRM's publication in the Federal Register. Comments received will be posted on Regulations.gov." Chairman Michael S. Selig is quoted: "Today's action is a critical step in the CFTC's ongoing efforts to ensure America remains the crypto capital of the world." The release states no RIN and no docket number. As of the date of this record the ANPRM had not appeared in the Federal Register, so the 60-day comment period had no start date.
entries.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9307-26, October 5, 2026 (cftc.gov, retrieved in full)
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges and trading venues, designated contract markets, futures commission merchants, retail crypto brokers, prediction-market platforms

entries.title: FinCEN withdraws two proposed digital-asset rules: the convertible virtual currency and unhosted wallet recordkeeping and reporting proposal, and the convertible virtual currency mixing special measure proposal
entries.facts: A FinCEN news release dated October 5, 2026, titled "FinCEN Announces Withdrawals of Proposed Digital Asset Related Rules," states that FinCEN is withdrawing two proposed rules: "a proposal that would have imposed recordkeeping, verification, and reporting requirements on certain transactions involving convertible virtual currencies and unhosted wallets" and "a proposal that would have imposed a special measure with regards to convertible virtual currency mixing." The release states: "FinCEN has considered the comments submitted in response to these proposals and is withdrawing them as part of the Trump Administration's deregulatory agenda and ongoing efforts to ensure digital asset regulations are fit-for-purpose." The release identifies the two withdrawal notices as Federal Register documents 2026-20430, "Requirements for Certain Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currency or Digital Assets; Withdrawal," and 2026-20429, "Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Convertible Virtual Currency Mixing; Withdrawal." The release states no RIN, no original Federal Register citation or date for either withdrawn proposal, and quotes no named official. As of the date of this record neither withdrawal notice had appeared in the Federal Register.
entries.source_label: FinCEN News Release, October 5, 2026 (fincen.gov, retrieved in full)
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, money services businesses, wallet and custody providers, mixing services, bank and fintech AML compliance teams
